title: Chapter 2 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Docker CLI, images, running containers, and container lifecycle.

questions.question: Which of these is the correct modern Docker command to list all containers?
questions.explanation: `docker container ls` is the modern management‑command style. `docker ps` is the old style, but still works. The modern style is preferred for consistency.

questions.question: What does `docker pull node:14` do?
options: Downloads the Node.js image tagged '14' from the registry to your local machine
Runs a Node.js container with version 14
Creates a new image based on Node 14
Builds an image from the current directory
questions.explanation: `docker pull` downloads an image. The tag `14` specifies the version. If the image already exists locally, it’s updated.

questions.question: If you run `docker pull ubuntu` without a tag, Docker will pull the newest available version.
questions.explanation: It pulls the image with the tag `latest`, which is a default tag – not necessarily the absolute newest version.

questions.question: Which command removes an image named 'myapp:1.0'?
questions.explanation: `docker rmi` (or `docker image rm`) removes images. `docker rm` is for containers.

questions.question: What is a dangling image?
options: An image that has been corrupted
An image that has no tag and no container references
An image that is still being pulled
An image that is larger than 1GB
questions.explanation: Dangling images are those with `<none>` as repository and tag, often leftover after a new build overwrites the old tag.

questions.question: What does the `-d` flag do in `docker run -d nginx`?
options: Deletes the container when it stops
Runs the container in detached (background) mode
questions.explanation: `-d` stands for detached. The container runs in the background and control returns to the terminal.

questions.question: You run `docker run -d --name web -p 4000:80 nginx`. How do you access the Nginx welcome page?
questions.explanation: The host port is 4000, container port is 80. You access via the host’s port on localhost.

questions.question: Container names must be unique across all containers (running and stopped) on the same host.
questions.explanation: Docker enforces uniqueness of container names. If you try to reuse a name, you’ll get an error until you delete the old container.

questions.question: The flag to automatically remove a container when it exits is `_____`.
questions.explanation: `--rm` is a convenient flag for temporary containers. After the main process exits, the container is automatically removed.

questions.question: What signal does `docker stop` send by default?
questions.explanation: `docker stop` sends SIGTERM, giving the process time to shut down gracefully. If it doesn’t respond in 10 seconds, it sends SIGKILL.

questions.question: How do you forcefully terminate a container named 'stubborn'?
questions.explanation: `docker kill` sends a SIGKILL immediately. Use it when `docker stop` doesn't work.

questions.question: Which command is used to start a container that was previously stopped?
questions.explanation: `docker start` resumes a stopped container with its original configuration. `docker run` creates a new container.

questions.question: `docker restart` is exactly the same as `docker stop` followed by `docker start`.
questions.explanation: `docker restart` stops and then starts the container. It’s a convenient shortcut for that sequence.

questions.question: You want to delete a stopped container called 'old-db'. What command do you use?
questions.explanation: `docker rm` (or `docker container rm`) removes a container. `docker rmi` is for images.

questions.question: To see the last 50 lines of a container’s logs and follow new ones, you would use `docker logs --tail 50 ___ mycontainer`.
questions.explanation: `-f` (or `--follow`) keeps the log stream open, showing new output as it’s written.

questions.question: What does `docker container prune` do?
questions.explanation: `docker container prune` deletes all stopped containers. It’s a quick cleanup command.

questions.question: Which command shows the top‑level help for Docker?
questions.explanation: Both `docker --help` and `docker -h` work to display the help information.

questions.question: The command `docker ps` shows only running containers by default.
questions.explanation: `docker ps` without flags lists running containers. `-a` includes stopped ones.

questions.question: You want to set an environment variable `DB_HOST=prod-db` inside a container at runtime. Which flag do you use?
questions.explanation: `-e` (or `--env`) sets environment variables. `-v` is for volumes.

questions.question: What happens if you try to remove an image that is used by a stopped container?
options: It succeeds and the container is also deleted.
It fails with an error because the image is in use.
It requires the `--force` flag but works otherwise.
questions.explanation: Docker prevents deletion of images that are referenced by any container (even stopped). You must remove the container first or use `-f`.

questions.question: Which command would you use to see the detailed configuration of your Docker engine?
questions.explanation: `docker info` displays extensive system information including storage driver, number of containers/images, and more.

questions.question: Once you pull an image, it will never be updated automatically even if you run `docker pull` again.
questions.explanation: Running `docker pull` again will check the registry for an updated version of the same tag and download it if different.
